samples.marker_line: Rifaien VM client: submits mutated self-copies; overlay is inert
evidence: Emulated only UPX decompression and branch repair with Unicorn, stopping at 0x428716 before import resolution. The decompressed entry transfers to CRT startup at 0x401130 and main at 0x4013a0.
Main calls GetModuleFileNameA, fopen(rb), fseek/ftell/malloc/fread to load its complete own image. It locates [[UNIQUE]], changes the next 16 bytes, and writes a random rifaien2-%s.exe copy.

The loop sleeps 30 seconds, chooses NODE1 through NODE7, posts file[], node and submit via curl_formadd and CURLOPT_HTTPPOST to http://wecan.hasthe.technology/upload, deletes that temporary copy, and repeats. The response does not feed command dispatch or payload execution.

The overlay starts at 0x14c00. A PE begins at 0x14c8b, with only 123426 bytes remaining, while its declared resource section alone requires 1939456 bytes. Imports/resources extend beyond EOF. No path from the self-submission code activates this trailer; it is included in the uploaded self-buffer.

The traced purpose is VM test submission. No victim-file infection, secret collection, remote command handling or persistence was established. This positive behavior evidence tips BENIGN despite the external labels; operator authorization and present endpoint ownership remain unknown.

Self-copy mutation, invalidated UPX checksums, repeated executable uploads and a truncated protector/implant prefix plausibly explain generic malware and sandbox labels. The fixed endpoint was attempted with forager but timed out; no downloaded code was executed.

samples.marker_line: Protected CLR implant: concealed commands and capture uploads
evidence: Native main extracts RT_RCDATA/__ using FindResourceA/LoadResource/LockResource/SizeofResource. Independently emulated the pure table initializer at 0x401300 and reproduced 1024-byte forward/reverse neighbor-byte decoding.

Decoding recovers a size-prefixed zlib stream: length 2576910, CLR prefix v4.0.30319, then managed PE at offset 14. The native host copies the managed bytes into a VT_UI1 SAFEARRAY and invokes _AppDomain::Load_3 through vtable slot 45 (0xb4), followed by reflected invocation.

The bootstrap reads resource _, calls Assembly.Load(byte[]), obtains its EntryPoint and invokes it. That resource is the real managed program, initially protected by fake method headers, flattened control flow, encrypted strings and delegate proxies.

A bounded data-only CIL interpreter recovered the 65892-byte method patch stream and 1650 field-to-method mappings. Strong-name public-key token 461d39c4a423da0b participates in key setup. Restored all 2610 method-header records and replaced 10898 delegate proxy calls.

Forager recovered prior reconstructed analysis artifacts with provenance. Independently reconstructed restored and resolved images matched those artifacts byte for byte. They are analysis reconstructions, not original distributed binaries.

Entry method 0x060002a8 reaches task runner ab2.2J2::nC6. Native startup, managed loader and the application task/delegate graph were traced without executing sample entry points or OS/network effects.

U7S.277::4nv receives text through 958.E65::rkB/WebClient.DownloadString. Task decoding and E42.6yQ::YdP select handlers. S7j.n4v constructor builds ProcessStartInfo, sets UseShellExecute=false, concealed filename/arguments, WindowStyle=1, and calls Process.Start.

M64::96t reads Clipboard.GetText and GetFileDropList; UTF8.GetBytes results enter 1cq.kJk::J3H/C75 archive insertion. Capture routines o55.721::m28 and 1s2 use Graphics.GetHdc and the BitBlt P/Invoke, producing image bytes.

HtQ::E2P/wN8 and 958.E65::F4j/c58 pass encoded archive/image bytes to 958.E65::48o; that method creates the HTTP request, gets its request stream, writes the supplied byte array and obtains the response.

Concealed remote task handlers combined with surveillance and outbound reports tip MALICIOUS. Commercial protection and individual HTTP/process APIs alone do not. Family attribution, virtualized C2/configuration strings and host authorization remain unresolved.

samples.marker_line: Login redirect page: relative navigation, no theft demonstrated
evidence: Inspected the entire 254-byte HTML and its JavaScript. A constant relative Login.php?sslchannel=true&sessionid=<token> string is assigned to page, then top.location=page navigates the containing window.

No obfuscation, form, credential source, send operation, executable stage, dependency or external host is present. All six existing notable traits accurately describe the script-only page, URL and navigation.

The destination cannot be fetched without the missing original origin. Forager hash recovery tried MalwareBazaar (not found), Triage (HTTP 500) and Malshare (404), without recovering surrounding content.

BENIGN describes the observed redirect component; it does not establish that its unavailable destination is harmless. A redirect captured alongside a phishing kit or a classifier overgeneralizing long SSL/session-looking tokens could explain the external malware label. The original page origin, linked login implementation and collection context are missing.

changes.unsupported_claim: UPX layout, writable sections and overlay entropy alone do not establish deliberate concealment or active unpacking of the trailer. Rifaien supplies a traced self-submission counterexample.
changes.preservation: All six required conditions, exclusions and confidence preserved. Description now asserts only physical layout. Removed attack mapping T1027.002 because geometry alone does not prove that technique. No technique-specific decoder, loader, mutation or upload detection was removed.
changes.consumers: Searched the exact ID and every ancestor selector in YAML before relocation: no consumers. Inspected relevant historical positive/boundary records and tested five independent attack files outside this batch; all original findings retained.

changes.supported_claim: Native byte-array assembly loading through the CLR AppDomain COM interface.
changes.generalization: Standard AppDomain IID in .rdata plus the traced byte-array preparation and Load_3 call sequence in .text. Stack offsets, helper/IAT addresses and relative calls vary; no sample names, hashes, URLs, exact sizes or payload family are required. Legitimate native CLR hosts may match accurately.

uncovered_behaviors: clipboard acquisition to archive and HTTP upload
coverage_gap.investigation: Native resource decoder and CLR activation traced; three managed layers extracted; encrypted method headers and delegate proxies independently reconstructed; original facts and decoded strings reviewed; recovered assemblies and embedded member rescanned. A native loading capability was added.
coverage_gap.limitation: Original scans see a native protector, not its decoded managed application. YAML cannot execute the substitution decoder, decompress the protected resource, restore encrypted CIL headers or resolve proxies. Recovered CIL facts expose neutral APIs without the source-to-sink bindings needed for portable hostile rules. Packing/API co-occurrence or a sample-specific ciphertext fingerprint would not justify hostile claims.
coverage_gap.classifier_disagreement: Original and reconstructed implant continue to classify BENIGN. Original score/confidence remains 0.99289215 with cls=0/lvl=-1; this is a false negative, not a malicious verdict. The scanner warns that model feature schema v18 predates engine v21.

validation.full_validation: Run make validate as the final action after this record and markers are written.

limitations: No sample entry point, child process, network effect or surveillance effect was executed. Runtime success and final C2 reachability are not asserted.

Original samples are not archives. The recovered bootstrap exposes one embedded managed PE; its findings were compared as well. Its DLL/.exe mismatch finding comes from the analysis filename and is not attributed to the distributed wrapper.
